</svg><text x="916" y="164" font-size="14" fill="#6b7280" text-anchor="start" font-weight="400">uniform reading gives each key 1/t —</text><text x="916" y="184" font-size="14" fill="#6b7280" text-anchor="start" font-weight="400">the count itself is a position signal</text><text x="916" y="204" font-size="14" fill="#6b7280" text-anchor="start" font-weight="400">(Haviv et al. 2022)</text><text x="660" y="268" font-size="15" fill="#6b7280" text-anchor="start" font-weight="400">permutation-equivariant without a mask; with it, position is inferred —</text><text x="660" y="290" font-size="15" fill="#6b7280" text-anchor="start" font-weight="400">never written down anywhere in the model</text><g class="fragment" data-fragment-index="1"><rect x="20" y="330" width="1200" height="56" rx="9" fill="#fff5f5" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-dasharray="7 5"/><text x="40" y="354" font-size="18" fill="#dc2626" text-anchor="start" font-weight="700">so the mask is enough to learn order.</text><text x="420" y="354" font-size="17" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="start" font-weight="400">What does writing the position down explicitly buy — and what does it cost at lengths never seen?</text><text x="40" y="378" font-size="15" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="start" font-weight="400">That is this week. The answer is not "order": it is extrapolation you can reason about, resolution at long range, and a bill.</text></g></svg>
